title: Finite generation of fixed fields for compatible finite actions
statement: Let $k\subseteq E$ be fields [def-weil-field, def-pc-field-extension], with $E=k(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ for some finite family. Let a finite group $H$ act on $k$ and $E$ by field automorphisms, and assume that for $a\in k$ and $h\in H$, the image of $h(a)$ in $E$ equals $h$ applied to the image of $a$. Define $k_0=k^H=\{a\in k:h(a)=a\ \forall h\in H\}$ and $F=E^H=\{x\in E:h(x)=x\ \forall h\in H\}$. Then $k_0\subseteq F$, both $k/k_0$ and $E/F$ are finite separable extensions, and both $E/k_0$ and $F/k_0$ are finitely generated as field extensions. Here finitely generated means generated as a field by a finite family, and finite separable means finite-dimensional with every element having separable minimal polynomial [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Neither action is required to be faithful; no geometric reducedness or integrality hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: For $a\in k_0$ and $h\in H$, compatibility gives $h(a)=a$ also in $E$. Hence $k_0\subseteq F$. The subsets $k_0$ and $F$ are subfields because automorphisms preserve sums, products, $0$, $1$, negatives and inverses.

Let $G_k$ and $G_E$ be the respective images of $H$ in the automorphism groups of $k$ and $E$. Each is a finite group acting faithfully, and an element is fixed by its image exactly when it is fixed by every element of $H$. Apply [lem-wf-finite-field-action-fixed-degree] to these two groups. Thus $k/k_0$ and $E/F$ are finite-dimensional and separable algebraic; no faithfulness of the original actions is used.

source.place: Tag 09I3 (lemma-galois-over-fixed-field), applied to the two automorphism images.

proof.text: By [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], choose a finite $k_0$-spanning family $u_1,\ldots,u_r$ of $k$. Adjoin it to the given finite field-generating family $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ of $E/k$, and call the combined family $z_1,\ldots,z_N$. The field $k_0(z_1,\ldots,z_N)$ contains $k$, since it contains every $k_0$-linear combination of the $u_j$, and then contains $E=k(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$. The reverse inclusion holds since all generators lie in $E$. Therefore $E=k_0(z_1,\ldots,z_N)$, proving finite generation of $E/k_0$.

source.place: Finite-dimensionality from Tag 09I3 (lemma-galois-over-fixed-field); explicit field-generator argument.

proof.text: For each $i$ let $O_i=\{h(z_i):h\in H\}$ and set $P_i(T)=\prod_{b\in O_i}(T-b)$. Each $h$ permutes $O_i$, so applying $h$ to the coefficients leaves $P_i$ unchanged. Thus all coefficients belong to $F$. Let $S$ be the finite set of all these coefficients and $C=k_0(S)\subseteq F$. Each $P_i$ is a monic polynomial of positive degree over $C$ and vanishes at $z_i$, so $z_i$ is algebraic over $C$. Since $k_0\subseteq C\subseteq E$ and the $z_i$ generate $E/k_0$, we have $E=C(z_1,\ldots,z_N)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension] to obtain that $E$ is finite-dimensional over $C$.

source.place: Tag 09I3 (lemma-galois-over-fixed-field), first proof paragraph (orbit polynomials); Tag 09GH (lemma-algebraic-finitely-generated).

proof.text: The field $C$ is Noetherian in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]: an ideal containing $x\ne0$ contains $x^{-1}x=1$, so its ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$. By [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], finite-dimensionality makes $E$ a finite $C$-module. Since $C\subseteq F\subseteq E$, $F$ is a $C$-submodule of $E$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] to obtain a finite $C$-spanning family $b_1,\ldots,b_m$ of $F$. The field $C(b_1,\ldots,b_m)$ contains every such linear combination and lies in $F$, so equals $F$. Consequently $F=k_0(S\cup\{b_1,\ldots,b_m\})$, generated by a finite set.

source.place: Tag 00IK (lemma-Noetherian-basic), submodule-finiteness assertion; explicit conversion from linear to field generators.
